title: Review: PKIX 2025-06-15
description:
Review: PKIX 2025-06-15. Library mode review covering correctness and API-contract risks.

Review confidence: 25% chance of missed bug.
Least confident areas: (1) pkix-path chain_walk policy tree machinery (RFC 5280 section 6.1.3-6.1.5 policy tree update/prune logic is ~500 lines of state-machine code with subtle counter semantics; reviewed structurally but did not trace every PKITS policy test case through the code). (2) Name constraint intersection logic in pkix-path (the NC permitted-set intersection and NcTypeMask bitmask tracking is correct by inspection but the edge cases around empty-intersection-for-a-type-that-was-constrained are subtle). (3) pkix-lint RFC lint implementations (skimmed for structural correctness but did not independently verify each lint predicate against the RFC text). (4) pkix-ct verify module (1380 lines, SCT verification — read structurally but did not trace Merkle proof verification step by step).
Would raise confidence if: (a) ran PKITS policy test suite against the policy tree code with instrumented assertions on tree state at each step, (b) fuzz-tested the name constraint intersection with pathological GeneralSubtrees inputs, (c) reviewed pkix-ct verify.rs against RFC 6962/9162 section by section.
notes:
## Review Confidence Calibration

Review confidence: 20% chance of missed bug.

Least confident areas:
- pkix-path/src/lib.rs policy tree state machine (RFC 5280 §6.1.3-6.1.5, ~500 lines)
- pkix-path/src/lib.rs name constraint intersection edge cases
- pkix-ct Merkle proof verification (reviewed structurally, not step-by-step vs RFC 6962 §2.1.1)
- pkix-lint OSCAL emit/parse round-trip

Would raise confidence if:
- Full line-by-line review of policy tree code with PKITS trace-through
- Fuzz-testing name constraint intersection with pathological inputs
- Step-by-step Merkle proof trace against RFC 6962

## Findings Summary (after dedup)

- P0 (must fix): 0
- P1 (should fix): 27 open
- P2 (worth fixing): 21 open
- P3 (polish/positive): 14 open
- Closed (duplicates): 8+2 pre-existing

## Positive Findings
- Error type design: #[non_exhaustive] everywhere, structured fields, DerError opaque newtype
- Test discipline: external oracles throughout, no self-testing
- Trust-domain callback architecture: clean separation of concerns
- Fail-closed extension handling: uniform across all crates
- Side-channel delegation to RustCrypto: correct
- No unsafe code: #![forbid(unsafe_code)] on all 22 crates
- No private key material held anywhere in the workspace
- No logging/debug output of sensitive data
